subject: mimicChest
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: treasure-chest mimic with a long tongue.
Style: Dungeons & Dragons.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a D&D-style treasure chest mimic in TypeScript — designing the box-shaped body with stubby clawed legs to give it a creature-like feel, plus a long tongue feature.

Now I'm working through the hinged lid as an open mouth lined with teeth, a fleshy pink-red interior, and a curling multi-joint tongue extending out front. I'm also figuring out eye placement, settling on partially-sunk eyeball spheres with iris decals set into the front panel, surrounded by a cracked-wood eyelid ring, before moving on to the wood-grain paint texture and metal bands.

Now I'm detailing the metal hardware (gilt lock plate with a keyhole, iron bands), the teeth as cone shapes along both rims, and the tongue's painted texture with drool drips following its curved path. I'm also deciding to repurpose the four legs as stubby tentacle-like limbs and scatter a few coins near the mouth as treasure bait, plus a subtle glow on the eyes. For the skeleton, I'm mapping the root to a spine-role hip joint, the jaw to a hinge at the back, and assigning the tongue to the tentacle role while the legs use the leg role.

Now I'm working out body dimensions and the lid hinge mechanics — building the lid in its closed position attached to a jaw bone, then posing it open by rotating around the x-axis, since a forward-facing bone tips downward with positive rotation degrees.

Legs will be simple stubby two-point chains from the body's bottom corners down to feet near the ground, rather than full IK chains, since they're too short to need multiple segments.

Now I'm curving the tongue outward from the mouth with a tapering catmull-rom path that narrows toward the tip, giving it a tentacle-like shape with 7 segments, letting the tip hover just above the floor so it could drip drool. I'm also planning the fleshy pink interior of the mouth as an inset box slightly smaller than the body cavity.

I'm designing the mouth as a solid wood body with a pink floor plate inset at the rim so the wood shows around the edge, plus teeth along the rim, painted gum ridges, and a dark red gullet ellipsoid sunk into the center. For the lid, I'm shaping an arched cross-section extruded along the width, with a matching pink flesh plate underneath visible when the lid opens.

Writing wood grain and plank seam shader logic...

Now I'm thinking through iron strap bands wrapping the body—trying to figure out the simplest geometry approach, maybe thin boxes forming a frame across the front and sides to look like reinforcing bands.

I also want a lock plate with a keyhole decal on the body front, and a matching hasp hanging from the lid. For the eyes, I'll embed two spheres on the body front panel with an SVG decal (yellow sclera, slit pupil) facing outward, maybe adding a subtle glow and a torus ring for a wooden eye socket detail.

I'm placing lower teeth as cones around the body rim path and upper teeth hanging from the lid rim, varying their length with randomness for a ragged look. For drool, I'll add a few thin pale strands between the teeth and a drip spike from the tongue tip down to the floor, then scatter gilt coin cylinders across the mouth floor.

I'm planning the surface textures now: a small gem octahedron on the tongue, plus decal textures for an eye, a keyhole lockplate, and scratched graffiti marks on the lid, keeping things simple with just three SVG textures. Now I'm setting up the imports from the builder API before writing the actual construction code.

Setting up the chest skeleton structure...

Adding grime shading and grain streaks for the wood texture, then starting on metal material definitions for iron, gilt, and flesh tones.

Writing flesh and tongue paint functions...

Still building body parts...

Now I'm setting up the lower jaw lid as a separate jointed bone, extruding its outline shape from the jaw pivot point with wood coloring and appropriate thickness.

Then I'm adding the flesh slab behind the lid, checking that its dimensions sit correctly against the body opening when the jaw is open rather than overlapping the closed-rim geometry, before moving on to add the uvula.

Still writing spike and strap code...

Adding corner brackets as iron boxes, then placing a gilt lock plate centered on the front, checking its width against the eye positions so they don't overlap, and shrinking both as needed to fit.

Now I'm positioning a keyhole decal on the plate, then building the hasp as a box hanging from the lid's front face edge so it reads correctly when open. Finally I'm placing the eye spheres with a gilded color and considering a decal for them.

For the eyes, I'm drawing an SVG with yellow sclera, orange iris, slit pupil, and highlight, projecting it as a decal onto the eye sphere facing outward, then adding a wooden eyelid as a thin torus ring around each eye lying flat against the surface with no extra rotation needed.

Now I'm setting up the leg positions, computing symmetric hip, knee, and foot coordinates for each side based on sx/sz signs and naming each leg by its front/back and left/right position before chaining the limb geometry together.

Still writing claw placement logic...

Now setting up the tongue as a tentacle chain with a tapering elliptical cross-section, rounded caps, and its own color.

For the drool, I'm adding a tapering spike from a point near the mouth down to the floor along with a small flattened puddle cylinder beneath it. Then I'm placing a glowing emerald gem partway along the tongue, plus several small gold coin cylinders scattered within the mouth floor inset for extra detail.

Now I'm laying out the teeth along a closed rectangular rim path inset slightly from the mouth corners, using an "along" helper to distribute them evenly and assigning explicit bone attachments for both upper and lower rows since the path itself has no bone reference. I'm skipping splinter details on the lid rim, and setting the jaw's pose rotation to tip it forward by -75 degrees, double-checking the bone's forward direction to make sure the tilt reads correctly.

Working through the rotation math about the X-axis to confirm negative degrees lifts the lid backward into an open position, which checks out — then adding small iron hinge brackets at the back top edge with their own bone cores.

Writing SVG code for the eye...

Now I'm planning a gold keyhole plate with an engraved border, plus a carved bone skull emblem on the lid's apex for fun detail, oriented so its normal faces upward.

I'll add two small tentacles at the back corners curling upward instead, and sort out the TypeScript import for the OutlinePoint type. For eyes I'll use a flat-shaded small sphere geometry, and for the tongue sweep I'll have the radius function return a tuple. Now I'm writing the module itself, aiming for roughly 350 lines, and double-checking the signature for the along-path callback and how spike points convert from a base point.

I'm also planning spike parameters including direction, length, radius, and color options, plus a decal helper for the eye texture with mirroring based on side, followed by a glow effect on that part. For the leg and tentacle flesh I'm designing a hybrid paint that blends wood and flesh textures using noise, so the pseudopods visually transition from wood to flesh.

Writing noise blend logic...
